terra.problem: The LORD tells Jeremiah to make the yoke; He does not hand it to him.
The text does not say everybody will see Jeremiah wearing the yoke.
The passage records the command to put on the yoke, but does not say Jeremiah puts it on.
The text says to send word through the envoys, not that Jeremiah has already sent it or that the kings have received it.
The text does not say the envoys carry the message home; it gives Jeremiah the instruction to send it through them.
The imagined homework line has the envoys leaving with the message, which the text does not report.
The statement that Pharaoh Neco was a king of Egypt needs a reference outside this passage.
The statement that Cyrus was a king of Persia needs a reference outside this passage.
The text does not say the message was popular. 'I'm sure' presents that as a conclusion rather than a tentative guess.
Calling life 'the goal of the whole thing' claims a comprehensive purpose the passage does not state.
The text does not say Jeremiah prevents the people from settling for doing nothing.
Saying the problem is not what God told the prophets goes beyond the text, which does not say what He told them.
The text does not say everybody wanted to hear the prophets' news.
The text does not say people liked the prophets' message or why they liked it.
Jeremiah's desire for the people to choose well is presented as fact rather than as Papa Dorin's inference.
The claim about what Jeremiah would rather see is an unmarked guess about his feelings.
The explanation is flat and generic: it restates the passage and summarizes the same point without Papa Dorin's voice.
The explanation is flat and generic, relying on a restatement and a summary rather than Papa Dorin's voice.
The passage does not say Jeremiah's answer was unpopular.
